Chania Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chania, Greece

Demolished. Chania's Jewish community existed under Venetian rule from 1204 to 1645 and gained further prominence under subsequent Ottoman rule, flourishing especially in the 15th and 16th centuries. Financial instability followed the Cretan uprising beginning in 1896, though the community persisted and even sheltered 200 refugees from Izmir in 1897 and hundreds more from the region during WWI. On May 20, 1944, 265 Jews were imprisoned for a week before being put aboard a ship at Heraklion; the few who survived in hiding left Chania after the war, mostly for Israel and the United States. The cemetery itself, presumed to date to the 13th century, has been completely lost — part of its former grounds now serves as a school parking lot, another part belongs to an olive oil company, and a local high school building sits on what was likely also cemetery land.
